title: Rethinking Key-Value Cache Compression Techniques for Large Language Model Serving
quote: The KV cache compression methods show negative computational efficiency in certain scenarios.
proves: Benchmarks KIVI, GEAR, H2O, StreamingLLM against FlashAttention+PagedAttention baselines: prefill speedup 0.86x (GEAR-4) and 0.58x (H2O) at TP=1; decode up to 1.34x but H2O falls to 0.69x at TP=2; gains vanish above batch 4 at 1024 tokens for StreamingLLM; outputs grow 1.55-1.76x longer on average, so end-to-end latency (FP16 11.4 s vs GEAR 13.4 s) can get worse; HF/TRL speedups judged unreliable.
does_not_prove: Does not test prefix caching, multi-turn reuse, speculative decoding, or Apple Silicon; uses research-code integrations rather than upstream engine features.
bearing: threatens: any compression idea whose gain is measured outside a paged engine; supports: output-length side effect as an unmeasured cost axis

title: SCBench: A KV Cache-Centric Analysis of Long-Context Methods
quote: sub-O(n) memory methods suffer in multi-turn scenarios.
proves: With shared context reused across turns/requests, eviction methods collapse: Llama-3.1-8B multi-request avg StreamingLLM 14.5, SnapKV 15.2, PyramidKV 15.3 vs full 37.2; Qwen2.5-72B SnapKV 3.3 vs 45.8. Query-dependent methods do well on first query, then lose accuracy. KIVI (quantization) holds up better (24.8). Quest drops 28.2 to 16.2 multi-request.
does_not_prove: Accuracy only; no throughput/latency inside a serving engine; does not propose a reuse-safe compression scheme.
bearing: threatens: query-aware eviction combined with prefix caching; supports: reuse-safe (query-agnostic, lossless-on-reuse) compression as a gap

title: KV Cache Compression, But What Must We Give in Return? A Comprehensive Benchmark of Long Context Capable Approaches
quote: Keeping the prefill process uncompressed is crucial for performance maintenance.
proves: 10+ methods across 7 long-context task categories: quantization performs decently everywhere; token dropping excels only on some tasks (e.g. coding); needle retrieval stays hard for prefill-time compression.
does_not_prove: No serving-engine throughput measured (A100 runs, Sys.Supports column is kernel availability only); no batching or reuse.
bearing: supports: quantization over eviction as the safer lossy axis; threatens: prefill-time eviction ideas

title: vLLM docs: Quantized KV Cache
quote: Per-attention-head quantization is currently available only with the Flash Attention backend
proves: Upstream vLLM ships fp8_e4m3 / fp8_e5m2 KV cache on CUDA/ROCm with per-tensor or per-head scales (scales default to 1.0 without calibration); no int4/int8 KV listed; sliding-window layers are more sensitive.
does_not_prove: Gives no memory or throughput numbers; quantization is the only compression mechanism listed (no eviction, no sparse attention for dense models).
bearing: supports: only fp8 quantization ships in vLLM; eviction/low-rank remain out of tree

title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache
quote: the key cache should be quantized per-channel.
proves: Keys per-channel, values per-token, 2-bit: 2.6x less peak memory, up to 4x larger batch, 2.35-3.47x throughput on their workload.
does_not_prove: Throughput measured in authors' HF-based stack, not a paged engine (D1 finds KIVI gains shrink and outputs lengthen 1.69x).
bearing: supports: asymmetric K/V bit allocation; threatens: novelty of plain K/V asymmetric quantization

title: KVQuant: Towards 10 Million Context Length LLM Inference with KV Cache Quantization
quote: < 0.1 perplexity degradation with 3-bit quantization on both Wikitext-2 and C4
proves: 3-bit KV with <0.1 PPL loss; LLaMA-7B at 1M context on one A100-80GB; custom kernels up to ~1.7x vs fp16 matrix-vector.
does_not_prove: Kernel-level speedups only; perplexity not task accuracy; no continuous batching or paged layout.
bearing: threatens: sub-4-bit KV quantization as novel

title: H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models
quote: Our implementation of H$_2$O with 20% heavy hitters improves the throughput over three leading inference systems
proves: Accumulated-attention eviction keeping 20% heavy hitters; up to 29x/29x/3x throughput vs DeepSpeed Zero-Inference, HF Accelerate, FlexGen.
does_not_prove: Baselines are offloading systems, not vLLM-class paged engines; needs attention scores that FlashAttention does not return (D18).
bearing: threatens: score-based eviction novelty; supports: score-free eviction for fused kernels

title: SnapKV: LLM Knows What You are Looking for Before Generation
quote: SnapKV can process up to 380K context tokens on a single A100-80GB GPU
proves: Prompt-end observation window picks KV to keep; 3.6x generation speed and 8.2x memory efficiency at 16K inputs.
does_not_prove: HF implementation; selection is query-dependent and fails on later queries over the same context (D2: multi-request 15.2 vs 37.2).
bearing: threatens: one-shot prompt compression with prefix reuse

title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
quote: keeping the KV of initial tokens will largely recover the performance of window attention
proves: Sink tokens plus a recent window give stable LM up to 4M tokens and 22.2x over sliding-window recomputation.
does_not_prove: Stability is perplexity, not retrieval; D2 shows multi-turn collapse; TRT-LLM's sink_token_length is now deprecated (D25).
bearing: supports: window+sink as cheap baseline; threatens: windowed cache novelty

title: PyramidKV: Dynamic KV Cache Compression based on Pyramidal Information Funneling
quote: PyramidKV matches the performance of models with a full KV cache while retaining only 12% of the KV cache.
proves: Layer-wise budgets (more in low layers) keep LongBench parity at 12% of KV.
does_not_prove: Accuracy only; per-layer variable budgets fragment paged memory (D19); multi-request collapse (D2: 15.3).
bearing: threatens: per-layer budget allocation novelty

title: Palu: Compressing KV-Cache with Low-Rank Projection
quote: Palu compresses KV-Cache by 50% while maintaining strong accuracy
proves: Low-rank cached latents reconstructed on the fly; up to 1.89x on RoPE attention module, 2.91x with quantization.
does_not_prove: Module-level speedup only; no paged-engine or batched serving numbers; reconstruction cost not quantified in abstract.
bearing: supports: low-rank KV in a real engine as unstudied

title: MiniCache: KV Cache Compression in Depth Dimension for Large Language Models
quote: achieves a remarkable compression ratio of up to 5.02x
proves: Cross-layer merging of similar adjacent-layer KV: up to 5.02x compression and ~5x throughput on LLaMA-2-7B ShareGPT with 4-bit.
does_not_prove: Not in any shipping engine seen; interaction with paged blocks and prefix sharing untested.
bearing: supports: cross-layer sharing inside paged allocator as gap

title: Quest: Query-Aware Sparsity for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
quote: Quest keeps track of the minimal and maximal Key values in KV cache pages.
proves: Page-level min/max key metadata picks top pages per query; up to 2.23x self-attention speedup, 7.03x inference latency reduction.
does_not_prove: Batch-1 style evaluation; keeps full KV in memory (no capacity win); D2 shows multi-request accuracy drop 28.2 to 16.2.
bearing: supports: page-granular sparsity matches paged blocks; threatens: page-summary top-k novelty

title: MagicPIG: LSH Sampling for Efficient LLM Generation
quote: TopK attention itself suffers from quality degradation in certain downstream tasks
proves: LSH sampling with CPU-resident hash tables and attention; up to 5x decode throughput; 54 ms/token at 96K on RTX 4090.
does_not_prove: Relies on discrete GPU+CPU split; unified-memory Macs remove the PCIe premise; not in any upstream engine.
bearing: threatens: naive top-k sparse attention; supports: rethinking offload designs for unified memory

title: ShadowKV: KV Cache in Shadows for High-Throughput Long-Context LLM Inference
quote: support up to 6$\times$ larger batch sizes
proves: Low-rank key cache plus offloaded values; up to 6x batch and 3.04x throughput on A100.
does_not_prove: Custom system, not vLLM/SGLang; CPU offload premise; no prefix sharing.
bearing: supports: low-rank K + sparse V as building block

title: RetroInfer: A Vector Storage Engine for Scalable Long-Context LLM Inference
quote: up to 4.4X decoding throughput over full attention at 120K context
proves: RetrievalAttention successor: wave index + GPU-CPU wave buffer; 4.4x over full attention at 120K, 12.2x over sparse baselines at 1M.
does_not_prove: Long single contexts on discrete GPUs; short-context batched serving and reuse not the target.
bearing: threatens: retrieval-attention-as-index ideas at long context

title: [RFC]: Support sparse KV cache framework (vllm-project/vllm #5751)
quote: Add the corresponding logic for updating block table mapping and manage the related allocated/free blocks
proves: General partial-eviction RFC for vLLM opened June 2024; still open with keep-open label; never merged; no maintainer verdict on block manager or prefix caching fit.
does_not_prove: Says nothing about why it stalled; targets v1 block manager that later changed.
bearing: supports: eviction absent from upstream vLLM after 2+ years

title: PagedEviction: Structured Block-wise KV Cache Pruning for Efficient Large Language Model Inference
quote: FlashAttention never returns the attention score during the inference process.
proves: Score-based eviction cannot run inside PagedAttention; block-wise eviction on vLLM 0.9.0 with no kernel changes gives ~37% throughput over full cache at budget 1024 (LLaMA-3.2-1B), ~10-12% lower TPOT, up to 3.1x in page-size ablation.
does_not_prove: Synthetic 1024-in/8192-out workload; no prefix caching or multi-turn; A100 only.
bearing: threatens: block-granular eviction in vLLM; supports: block-size vs eviction granularity tradeoff

title: KV-Compress: Paged KV-Cache Compression with Variable Compression Rates per Attention Head
quote: evicts contiguous KV blocks within a PagedAttention framework
proves: Variable per-head eviction fragments paged memory so savings vanish unless blocks are evicted contiguously; vLLM integration up to 5.18x throughput via larger batches.
does_not_prove: Fork, not upstream; no prefix caching or multi-turn accuracy.
bearing: threatens: per-head eviction in vLLM; supports: fragmentation as the core system problem

title: vToken: Token-Level Virtualization for Reclaimable KV Caches
quote: This mismatch causes intra-block fragmentation, leaving a large fraction of allocated KV memory unreclaimable.
proves: Token eviction inside fixed-size blocks leaves memory unreclaimable; vToken in vLLM cuts retained blocks 27.2-72.3% vs naive evict, up to 1.37x SLA throughput, up to 2x concurrency.
does_not_prove: Abstract does not cover prefix caching (search snippet said shared-prefix blocks are excluded, unverified); CUDA only.
bearing: threatens: eviction-reclaim layers in vLLM (very recent, Aug 2026)

title: Zipage: Maintain High Request Concurrency for LLM Reasoning through Compressed PagedAttention
quote: We propose a comprehensive scheduling strategy and support prefix caching and asynchronous compression for Compressed PagedAttention.
proves: Token eviction combined with PagedAttention plus prefix caching and async compression; ~95% of full-KV accuracy at >2.1x speedup on math reasoning.
does_not_prove: Own engine; reasoning workloads only; how shared prefixes are kept intact is not in the abstract.
bearing: threatens: eviction+prefix-caching co-design for reasoning

title: SGLang docs: HiSparse: Hierarchical Sparse Attention
quote: HiSparse currently requires PD disaggregation mode.
proves: SGLang ships top-k sparse decode with a small GPU hot buffer and full KV in host memory, but only for trained-sparse models (DeepSeek Sparse Attention, DeepSeek V4, MiniMax M3), decode instance only.
does_not_prove: Does not apply post-hoc sparsity to dense models like Qwen3; no numbers on page.
bearing: supports: shipped sparse attention is architecture-trained, not post-hoc; post-hoc sparsity remains research-only

title: SGLang docs: Quantized KV Cache
quote: Currently, only per-tensor (scalar) scaling factors are supported.
proves: SGLang ships fp8_e5m2/fp8_e4m3 KV (per-tensor scales, default 1.0) and experimental nvfp4/fp4_mx; without fused dequant performance can be extremely slow; NVFP4 path excludes speculative decoding, PD disaggregation, hierarchical KV cache, LMCache.
does_not_prove: No throughput numbers; CUDA only.
bearing: supports: quantized KV vs spec decode / hierarchical cache interaction as open

title: DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp in vLLM: Fine-Grained Sparse Attention in Action
quote: DSA's lightning indexer along with sparse attention presents challenges in continuous batching and paged attention.
proves: vLLM's only shipped sparse attention is model-native DSA: separate indexer K cache buffers, per-block (non-contiguous) indexer layout, separate prefill/decode indexer paths, fp8 MLA cache 656 bytes/token.
does_not_prove: Says nothing about prefix caching; post-hoc sparse methods for dense models not covered.
bearing: supports: trained-sparsity is the shipped path; threatens: claims that sparse attention is absent from engines

title: TensorRT-LLM KvCacheConfig reference
quote: Size of the attention window for each sequence. Only the last tokens will be stored in the KV cache.
proves: TRT-LLM ships KV dtype fp8 / fp8_ds_mla / nvfp4, block reuse, and per-layer max_attention_window; sink_token_length is a deprecated field; no eviction or sparse-attention fields.
does_not_prove: Does not document how windows interact with block reuse or quantized KV.
bearing: supports: StreamingLLM-style sinks being retired from a production engine

title: [FR] Make GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS the default or add runtime warning for missing quantized FA kernels (llama.cpp #24485)
quote: Dramatically worse prefill speed (25-45x slower in our tests)
proves: llama.cpp quantized K/V types (e.g. q8_0 K, q4_0 V) silently fall back to CPU attention on CUDA builds lacking all-quants FA kernels; closed as not planned.
does_not_prove: Single user report; CUDA build, not Metal; does not measure Metal quantized-KV kernels.
bearing: supports: quantized-KV kernel coverage as a hidden cost

title: mlx-lm mlx_lm/models/cache.py
quote: def __init__(self, group_size: int = 64, bits: int = 8):
proves: mlx-lm ships QuantizedKVCache (group 64, default 8-bit, step 256) and RotatingKVCache(max_size, keep) for window+sink; batch classes are BatchKVCache and BatchRotatingKVCache only, with no quantized batch cache.
does_not_prove: No eviction, low-rank, or sparse attention classes; no quality/speed data.
bearing: supports: quantized KV + batching gap on Apple Silicon

title: mlx-lm mlx_lm/server.py
quote: requests are served one at a time. Default: None (full precision)
proves: mlx-lm server exposes --kv-bits/--kv-group-size/--quantized-kv-start, but setting --kv-bits disables batching so requests run one at a time.
does_not_prove: Does not say why (likely no quantized batch cache); no measurements.
bearing: supports: batched quantized KV on MLX as an open, measurable gap

title: vllm-metal v0.30.0 release notes
quote: serving always uses paged attention
proves: vllm-metal rejects fp8, int8_per_token_head, nvfp4 kv-cache-dtype at startup because Metal stores paged KV in model dtype; TurboQuant is the alternative; hybrid GDN prefix caching experimental.
does_not_prove: Exact release date not shown; user runs vLLM 0.31.0 so check plugin version.
bearing: supports: vLLM fp8 KV path unavailable on the user's hardware

title: vllm-metal docs: TurboQuant KV cache compression
quote: a Walsh–Hadamard rotation followed by per-block quantization
proves: vllm-metal ships TurboQuant KV (default K q8_0, V q3_0): 2.56x to 4.92x smaller on a Qwen3-0.6B-shaped cache; keys more sensitive than values; head dim 64/128/256; no MLA; GDN state stays fp16.
does_not_prove: Gives no throughput, step time, or TPOT numbers and does not mention prefix caching or speculative decoding.
bearing: supports: measuring TurboQuant step time and batch-size effect on M-series as an unmeasured gap

title: NVIDIA kvpress
quote: By default, KVPress applies compression during the prefilling phase.
proves: Main eviction-benchmark library is built on HF transformers; decoding-time compression is a wrapper limited to ScorerPresses.
does_not_prove: No serving engine, paged layout, or batching; isolation-only measurements.
bearing: supports: most eviction results are isolation-only

title: MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
quote: MagicDec first identifies the bottleneck shifts with increasing batch size and sequence length.
proves: Draft with sparse KV cache attacks the KV bottleneck at large batch and long context; up to 2.51x for Llama3.1-8B at batch 32-256.
does_not_prove: Multi-GPU, long-context; not shown in an upstream engine; small-context regime differs.
bearing: supports: compressed-KV draft for spec decoding

title: QuantSpec: Self-Speculative Decoding with Hierarchical Quantized KV Cache
quote: employs a hierarchical 4-bit quantized KV cache
proves: Self-speculative draft uses 4-bit weights and hierarchical 4-bit KV (INT4/INT8 split) with >90% acceptance, ~2.5x speedup, ~1.3x less memory than sparse-KV self-spec baselines.
does_not_prove: Long-context batch-1 focus; not in vLLM/mlx-lm; Apple co-authors but no Metal serving numbers in abstract.
bearing: threatens: quantized-KV self-speculation novelty; supports: porting to MLX as measurable
